clue.text: Not exactly a well-earned rest

parts.note: time off work because of illness is a rest, but not one earned by hard labour or long service

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that their break hardly counts as a deserved holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence from work granted on medical grounds is a break, though not a reward for effort.

clue.text: Bush growing wild around river, maybe?

definitions.text: Bush growing wild around river, maybe?

indicators.note: around means the letters are placed on either side
growing wild means running uncontrolled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Scrub spreading untamed beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' rearranges BUSH to SHUB, and 'around' sets it round R; the whole clue also describes the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems, is a bush.

clue.text: Tall structure visible from main Place, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A tower seen from the town's central square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MAIN PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-standing bell tower, as in Italian towns, is a tall structure.

clue.text: Athlete's woolly reaching well below the hips?

definitions.meaning: a track and field competitor who leaps for distance

definitions.text: woolly reaching well below the hips?
definitions.meaning: a woolly is a knitted sweater, here an extended one

explanation.walkthrough: A woolly is a knitted pullover; a lengthy one is a long sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A field-event competitor leaping for distance, and an extended knitted pullover.

clue.text: Girl mostly stifling sob -it's synthetic

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece is enclosed by another
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A girl tries to hold back tears over man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ALICE to ALIC, and 'stifling' puts CRY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This plastic-based fibre is man-made rather than natural.

clue.text: Fellow's left attractive engraving

indicators.note: 's left reads as has left, so that letter departs

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: A man has left behind a lovely print.
explanation.walkthrough: 's left' removes F from FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a design bitten into metal by acid is a kind of engraving.

clue.text: Cold-blooded poisoner given support by firm

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is an undergarment giving support

explanation.surface: A ruthless murderer gets backing from a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded poisoner' reads as a heartless killer, but it is a venomous reptile; reptiles are literally cold-blooded.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake is a reptile, hence cold-blooded, and kills with poison.

clue.text: Cloak covering head

definitions.meaning: a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders
a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless shoulder cloak, and a headland projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Worker always busy on church in wood

parts.note: a worker bee is proverbially busy

explanation.surface: A tireless labourer at the church out in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous tree with smooth grey bark, and its timber.

clue.text: Overthrowing a despot in New Zealand?

indicators.note: overthrowing turns things upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Toppling a tyrant somewhere far down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrowing' rearranges A DESPOT IN; the question mark shows New Zealand is one example of the places opposite Britain on the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia and New Zealand are known in Britain as the lands diametrically opposite on the globe.

clue.text: Old empire-builder managed to secure recognition of merit

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An ancient imperialist contrived to win an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Rome built one of history's great empires.

clue.text: Tie Prince designed, one winning award?

indicators.note: something designed is shaped anew, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A neckwear design by a prince is honoured with a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the letters of TIE PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given a prize is its receiver, the one it goes to.

clue.text: No more than one drink? Perhaps!

definitions.text: No more than one drink? Perhaps!

parts.words: No more than one drink? Perhaps!
parts.note: the clue describes something that is merely one example of a drink, a single wine among many

explanation.surface: Someone vows to have just the one drink, but doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a promise to stop after one glass; the cryptic reading is that this French red is just one drink, with 'Perhaps' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A light red wine from Burgundy is a single instance of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Sharp blow will make central heating work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A hard thump will get the boiler going.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, sharp downward strike with the hand or an axe goes by this name.

clue.text: Anger occasioned by culling of marine mammals?

definitions.text: Anger occasioned by culling of marine mammals?

parts.words: Anger occasioned by culling of marine mammals?
parts.note: wax is old slang for a temper, read as the rage felt about hunting seals

explanation.walkthrough: To be in a wax is a British expression for being angry; the clue reads the stationery item as fury over seal hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Red resin melted to close letters is read as a fury about seals.

clue.text: Earth-shaking content of case is microfilmed

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds within, so the run sits inside these words

explanation.surface: The evidence on microfilm in a court case is momentous.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthquakes are studied by seismology; the adjective also means momentous.

clue.text: What wounded duellist may do in two-seater?

definitions.meaning: a duellist cut in a fight will afterwards show a mark
a small fast car with two seats

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer says what a duellist does with a mark left by a wound: displays it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounded fighter may show off a mark; a fast two-seat car is a sporty roadster.

clue.text: Believed to appear in programme only on special occasion, they say

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.words: to appear in programme only on special occasion
parts.note: to guest is to make a one-off appearance on someone else's show

explanation.surface: A performer reportedly thought to turn up only for special broadcasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something without proof is to surmise or think it so.

clue.text: Archer fish, say

parts.note: the Archer and the Fishes are zodiac emblems, Sagittarius and Pisces

explanation.walkthrough: An archer fish is a real species that spits water at insects, but here Archer and Fish are two zodiac emblems.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius the Archer and Pisces the Fishes are two of the twelve zodiac constellations.

clue.text: They'll usually remove caps and put on protective headgear

definitions.meaning: bottle tools take the metal tops off bottles
the first two batsmen in cricket wear helmets

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen face the fast new ball, so they put on helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle tools lever off caps, and the batsmen starting a cricket innings wear helmets.

clue.text: Robbery at Cambridge preceded by verbal abuse

indicators.note: preceded by puts the following piece in front

parts.note: stick is British slang for criticism or abuse
up means in residence at a university such as Cambridge

explanation.surface: A heist at a university, after a slanging match.
explanation.walkthrough: Students are said to be 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge while in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed hold-up in which a robber demands valuables at gunpoint.

clue.text: Items associated with Eton College, classical art

parts.note: COLL is a standard abbreviation for college
ars is Latin, the classical language, for art

explanation.surface: Things linked with a famous school, and ancient art.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton, the English boarding school, gave its name to a broad stiff white neckpiece worn by its boys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton type is a wide starched neckband traditionally worn by pupils there.

clue.text: Bank less obscured by mist, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a clearing bank, one handling cheque settlement

explanation.definitionFit: A clearing bank settles cheques; comparative of unclouded means more transparent.

clue.text: Australian can pipe

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang a can of beer is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Australians call a beer can by this name, and a pipe is a hollow cylinder.

clue.text: Aristocrat presenting heraldic device to cricket side

parts.note: a bar is a horizontal band on a coat of arms
the on side is the leg side of the field in cricket

explanation.surface: A nobleman gives his coat of arms to a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, also called leg side, is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank of the British peerage is a nobleman's title.

clue.text: Awful pre-recorded entertainment in today's vein, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe says the letters could take another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grim television fare, perhaps in the style of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the letters of TODAYS VEIN; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruesome horror film released on cassette was the 1980s tabloid term for awful home entertainment.

clue.text: Areas for storing cylindrical spars

definitions.meaning: enclosures for storage, as in timber stores
the round poles slung across a ship's mast to hold sails

explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed storage grounds, and the round poles across a mast that carry square sails.

clue.text: Pack given by bridge-player to left-hand opponent

parts.note: South is one of the four bridge seats, abbreviated S
taken as written
West sits to South's left at bridge, abbreviated W

explanation.surface: A card is handed by one bridge player to the rival seated on their left.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge seats are named by compass points; South's left-hand opponent is West.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things away neatly in a space is to stash them.

clue.text: Play running for a limited period?

definitions.meaning: a Harold Pinter drama of 1960 bears this title
a stand-in manager or government is in charge only temporarily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests a theatre run, but here it means being in charge, as a temporary government does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinter wrote a play of this name, and a temporary or interim government is so described.

clue.text: Comedian has little hesitation in making bet

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A joker pauses briefly before placing a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake placed on an uncertain outcome is a gamble.

clue.text: Frenchman initially wanted to begin again

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's first wish was a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume or restart something is to start it once more.

clue.text: Father's writing about old times in Rye — endless fits of laughter

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters wrap the rest

parts.note: Pa is father, with the possessive S

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: Rye is taken as written, an English town
X is the multiplication sign for times
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Dad's account of former days in Rye ends in helpless laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RYE to RY, and 'in' puts O and X inside it to make ROXY; 'about' has PAS and MS wrap that, giving PA ROXY S MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden violent outbursts, as of laughter or coughing, are convulsions.
